mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-8.7 to -12.3). This momentum reflects an ongoing contraction in discretionary mobility that is expected to persist absent a reversing shock, pushing the next 28-day mean further below the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the 28-day trailing mean despite the four-week decline streak, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES (e.g. the -9.1 point fall from t-3w to t-2w) signals renewed remote-work mandates or tightened indoor-gathering rules. Such policy tightening typically precedes reduced retail footfall as people minimize non-essential outings, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -13.6 to -22.7 between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 8 points, the policy-tightening mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Joint declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate reduced commuting-linked trip chains (e.g. after-work shopping, lunch-break errands). When both series fall together, their combined suppression of incidental retail visits compounds, producing a larger drop in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both at four-week lows at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline further despite simultaneous multi-week lows in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL (2.7 to 4.0 over four weeks) combined with falling TRANSIT suggests a behavioral retreat toward home-centered activity, consistent with risk-averse responses to a winter COVID resurgence. This home-bias is expected to continue suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as long as the underlying wave persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.7 to 4.0 while TRANSIT fell from -17.7 to -22.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds upward while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and TRANSIT stays depressed, the home-bias behavioral mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed roughly flat-to-slightly positive (9.3 to 11.9) while RETAIL_REC fell, indicating a substitution pattern where households maintain essential shopping but cut discretionary retail and recreation trips. This substitution behavior is expected to persist in the near term, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between 9.3 and 11.9 while RETAIL_REC fell from -8.7 to -12.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM move in the same direction over the next week (e.g. both rise together), the essential-versus-discretionary substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from +20.3 to -8.0 over four weeks, consistent with the seasonal transition into colder November weather in Lombardy. This seasonal shift away from outdoor activity reduces adjacent foot traffic to retail and recreation venues located near parks and open-air commercial strips, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 20.3 to -8.0 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite PARKS remaining negative, the seasonal outdoor-displacement hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossed from positive to negative territory between t-1w and t-0w (6.7 to -8.0), marking a threshold where cold-weather onset becomes behaviorally binding. Once PARKS turns negative, it signals that outdoor leisure substitutes have been exhausted, and combined outdoor-and-indoor recreation spending (captured by RETAIL_REC) drops further over the subsequent two weeks as people curtail outings generally rather than shifting them indoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from positive to negative value week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS went from 6.7 at t-1w to -8.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the two weeks following PARKS turning negative, the threshold-crossing seasonal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside a rise in RESIDENTIAL suggest that renewed public-health measures (e.g. expanded Green Pass requirements, indoor capacity limits) are jointly discouraging both commuting and leisure travel in Lombardy. In a tightening-restriction regime, this policy-driven interaction between commuting and residence-time proxies is expected to compound and depress RETAIL_REC over the full four-week horizon, but only while restrictions remain in force.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall while RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w WORKPLACES=-12.1, TRANSIT=-22.3, RESIDENTIAL=4.0 all consistent with restrictive regime
failure_condition: If restrictions are confirmed in force but RETAIL_REC does not decline further over the next four weeks, or if the three-way co-movement pattern dissolves without RETAIL_REC recovering, the policy-interaction hypothesis is rejected.
